stories.headline: U.S., Cuba shouting match derails debate at UN
stories.deck: The row broke out during debate on a resolution calling for an end to the U.S. embargo on its communist-led neighbour, a non-binding measure which Cuba has put forward every year since 1992
stories.bodyText:
A furious shouting match between representatives of the United States and Cuba prompted the temporary suspension of debate at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday (October 27, 2026).
The row broke out during debate on a resolution calling for an end to the U.S. embargo on its communist-led neighbour, a non-binding measure which Cuba has put forward every year since 1992.
The debate this year, however, is taking place amid a major new pressure campaign by Washington against Cuba, including an oil blockade and broad sanctions that have severely crippled Cuba's economy.
As U.S. Ambassador Mike Waltz was addressing the General Assembly, Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez objected to the remarks and walked up to the podium, demanding that the speech be halted.
Mr. Waltz, while arguing for the resolution to be rejected, had been criticising repression of Cuban citizens by the communist government.
"This is the United Nations. This isn't your communist dictatorship. You cannot silence me," Mr. Waltz shouted, demanding that Mr. Rodriguez and other Cuban diplomats back away.
"You are a liar!" Mr. Rodriguez shouted back.
The chair briefly suspended the session and instructed both countries’ representatives to return to their places, after which Mr. Waltz was allowed to continue.
Cuba has accused Washington of launching an "unprecedented" pressure campaign this year to persuade countries to oppose the resolution, which has traditionally had overwhelming backing.
Last year, the resolution received 165 votes in favor, seven against and 12 abstentions, its weakest level of support in two decades.
A vote on this year's resolution is expected sometime on Wednesday (October 28, 2026).
The row also comes days after U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged Cubans to discreetly work with the CIA to end the island's communist government.

stories.headline: Rubio joins Trump on campaign trail days before U.S. midterms
stories.deck: Donald Trump called Marco Rubio on stage at his campaign rally in Corpus Christi, Texas, remarking: “He’s so popular”
stories.bodyText:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio made a rare appearance on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) alongside President Donald Trump on the midterms campaign trail, visiting an oil tanker filled with Venezuelan crude just days before the crucial vote.
Mr. Rubio and Vice President J.D. Vance are widely viewed as top contenders to carry the Republican Party into its post-Trump era in the 2028 election.
But while Mr. Vance has been crisscrossing the country in recent weeks to rally support ahead of the November 3 polls, it is very unusual for the top U.S. diplomat to engage in such domestic political trips.
On Tuesday (October 27, 2026), Mr. Trump called Mr. Rubio on stage at his campaign rally in Corpus Christi, Texas, remarking: “He’s so popular.”
“We love Marco,” he added, beckoning Mr. Rubio to join him at the podium as the crowd chanted Mr. Rubio’s name.
A State Department official said Mr. Rubio was travelling with Mr. Trump in his capacity as National Security Advisor. He is the first person to hold both key foreign policy jobs since Henry Kissinger.
“He needs time with the President on all kinds of issues. The president will be on the go, so being on the plane with him gives (Rubio) a chance to talk to him about these items,” the U.S. official added on condition of anonymity.
While the official did not elaborate on the nature of these issues, their comments come against the backdrop of wars in the West Asia and Ukraine — as well as elections in Israel and the upcoming vote in the United States.
Mr. Rubio, who made a run for President in the 2016 election, has yet to say if he would throw his hat in the ring again in 2028.
Mr. Trump remains a dominant figure in the Republican party, and the 80-year-old has yet to endorse a successor.
Until now, Mr. Rubio, the first Hispanic and first fluent Spanish speaker to be the top U.S. diplomat, has steered clear of the campaign trail.
He has instead focused on a series of international trips — including visits to Uzbekistan and India last week.
He is also set to host a meeting of G20 Foreign Ministers in Atlanta, Georgia, on Friday (October 30, 2026) and Saturday (October 31, 2026).
Venezuelan oil
Mr. Trump and Mr. Rubio’s showcasing of an oil tanker carrying one million barrels of Venezuelan crude comes as affordability remains a top worry for American households grappling with steeper costs of gasoline and other goods.
The oil, Mr. Trump said, is set to be processed at Texas refineries.
Relations between Washington and Caracas have warmed after the United States toppled longtime leader Nicolas Maduro in a military operation in January.
Mr. Maduro’s Vice President Delcy Rodriguez took power after his ouster and has been complying with Trump’s demands for Caracas to open its energy industry to American companies.
Mr. Trump is hoping this showcase of supply from Venezuela will bolster support from voters, vowing that gasoline and diesel costs will soon cool.
Global oil prices have surged since U.S.-Israel strikes targeting Iran in late February triggered Tehran’s retaliation in blocking off a key route of energy transit, the Strait of Hormuz.
This has translated into higher costs at the gasoline pump and sparked a surge in transportation fees for businesses, threatening further spillover into consumer prices.
Republicans are wary that voter anger over inflation, stoked by Trump’s launch of war on Iran, could trigger a “blue wave” of Democrats winning in the midterms.
The U.S. leader has since been working to rally loyal supporters who often stay home when he is not on the ballot, as Republicans push to retain control of both chambers of Congress.
Mr. Trump has held near-daily rallies across the country over the past month.
His third visit to Texas in the past month reflects Republican concerns, as polls show a close Senate race in a state that has stayed solidly Republican for more than 30 years.

stories.headline: Oil price today: Brent crude holds firm at $115 per barrel, WTI trades at $100
stories.deck: After the Houthis announced a missile strike, Brent crude prices jumped to $115 a barrel, intensifying fears of oil supply disruptions from the conflict-laden Middle East. Additionally, a slight uptick in US oil inventories influenced trader responses. With expectations that OPEC+ will stick to existing output targets in their next assembly, the landscape of the oil market remains increasingly…
stories.bodyText:
Oil prices edged higher again on Wednesday, with Brent crude crossing $115 a barrel after declining in previous sessions. The rebound came after Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi group claimed a missile strike on Saudi Arabia’s largest oil refinery, reviving concerns over oil supplies from the Middle East amid the ongoing conflict involving Iran and its proxies.
Brent crude gained $1.22, or 1.07%, to trade at $115.10, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose $0.96, or 0.96%, to $100.90.
The Houthis on Tuesday said that they targeted the refinery, which has a processing capacity of 550,000 barrels per day. The claimed strike marked an escalation in their attacks against Saudi Arabia, the world's second-largest crude producer. Saudi authorities had not immediately confirmed the attack.
The latest gains followed a decline of nearly $2 in oil prices on Tuesday, when talks in the Middle East helped ease concerns over supply disruptions. The reported strike brought those concerns back into focus.
Expectations of higher crude inventories in the US provided another factor for the oil market to consider. US crude stockpiles increased by around 15,000 barrels in the week ended October 23, according to a Reuters poll of eight analysts.
On the production front, OPEC+ members are expected to maintain their December oil output targets at Sunday's meeting, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters. The expected decision is in line with market expectations.
Output in most of the group's seven core members, Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman, is already below their respective production targets.
Meanwhile, Russia's crude oil shipments from its Baltic and Black Sea ports could decrease next month, traders said.
The potential decline comes as Russian domestic refiners prepare to increase diesel production following a deal with Washington this month.
Oil prices have remained volatile as the Middle East crisis enters its eighth month. However, the latest spike remains below the $126-per-barrel peak recorded earlier in the crisis.

briefs.headline: Flavio Bolsonaro reaches U.S., say reports citing sources
briefs.deck: Two media houses, each citing an unnamed source close to the matter, said Flavo Bolsonaro had arrived in the U.S. on October 27
briefs.bodyText:
Defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro left Brazil for the United States despite a court order banning him from exiting the country, U.S. media reported on Tuesday October 27, 2026).
CNN and the Washington Post, each citing an unnamed source close to the matter, said Mr. Bolsonaro had arrived in the U.S. late Tuesday (October 27, 2026). Where he landed remains unknown.
The son of jailed ex-leader Jair Bolsonaro lost the presidential election Sunday (October 25, 2026) to incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and refused to concede defeat.
The right-wing senator on Monday (October 26, 2026) said a Supreme Court justice had ordered him to hand over his passports. Mr. Bolsonaro is under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering, and, with his election loss is also set to lose parliamentary immunity.
The U.S. State Department said Tuesday (October 27, 2026) it would issue visas to Mr. Bolsonaro and his family, without confirming his travel plans.
A police source told AFP that the senator’s Brazilian and diplomatic passports had been cancelled, adding that “there is no formal record of Flavio Bolsonaro leaving the country.”
But he has held Italian nationality since 2023, according to an Italian parliamentary document seen by AFP.
Mr. Bolsonaro’s campaign manager Rogerio Marinho expressed shock over reports that the defeated candidate had fled Brazil.
“We still don’t have any news about his whereabouts,” he told reporters Tuesday (October 27, 3036) in Brasilia.
“I received a text message from him this morning, where he said he would let some time pass today and then would talk with us, and that was it,” Mr. Marinho said.
“That was the only communication we had.”
‘Shameful’
Mr. Lula called fleeing the country a “shameful” act.
“A person who sneaks out of their country must have something to hide. The act of leaving Brazil is shameful,” he remarked in Brasilia during his 81st birthday celebration.
Mr. Bolsonaro said Monday (October 26, 2026) that the ban on his exit from Brazil amounted to a scare tactic.
“I never had any intention of leaving the country,” he said in a video posted on Instagram.
U.S. President Donald Trump, a close ally of Jair Bolsonaro, on Monday (October 26, 2026) said Brazil’s elections were “rigged” following the defeat of Bolsonaro junior.
Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro brother Eduardo Bolsonaro, a U.S.-based former lawmaker, maintains close ties with the White House.
Last week, he told a U.S. podcast that Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro should leave Brazil in the event of electoral defeat, given the active probes into his activities.
In his Monday statement, Mr. Lula’s challenger also said he would lead the opposition to the leftist government.
Following Mr. Lula’s victory with 51.8% of the vote, Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro said he would seek to annul the result, citing the decision to extend polling hours over transportation difficulties that prevented some citizens from voting.
Mr. Lula had requested the extension, as had Bolsonaro over bad weather in parts of the country.
In his father’s footsteps
All bets were on a Mr. Bolsonaro win after he came out on top in the first round of elections earlier this month.
He campaigned on a pledge to liberate his father, who is under house arrest for coup-plotting after his own electoral loss to Mr. Lula in 2022.
Mr. Jair Bolsonaro never conceded defeat and left the country on the eve of his rival’s inauguration, only returning to Brazil three months later.
Separately, on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), the Supreme Court ordered police to investigate alleged foreign funding of Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro’s campaign and other interference from abroad such as social media “manipulation.”
Mr. Lula’s campaign complained about election interference by Meta, the parent company of WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram, claiming “algorithmic manipulation.”
Meta denies taking any actions to favour one side in the election, but previously said that some of Mr. Lula’s campaign ads had been mistakenly deactivated due to technical errors.

briefs.headline: Create awareness on property transfer among elders: Karnataka HC to govt
briefs.deck: Create awareness on property transfer among elders: HC to govt
briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: The High Court has suggested that the state government may have to consider appropriate measures to create awareness among senior citizens about the legal consequences of transferring or relinquishing property during their lifetime. . Justice Suraj Govindaraj said this after noticing the rising number of cases under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act. . The court said that the state government may consider whether the existing safeguards under the Senior Citizens Act are being effectively implemented and whether further measures, consistent with the Act and other applicable laws, are necessary to strengthen awareness and protection. . “Such awareness may address the importance of understanding the nature and effect of documents before execution, the desirability of recording any intended obligation to provide maintenance or care, the risks of transferring the principal source of livelihood or security, and the remedies available under the law if the transfer results in deprivation of maintenance or support,” Justice Suraj Govindaraj said. . In the case at hand, the petition pertained to the order passed by the Assistant Commissioner, Bhadravathi, setting aside the release deed executed by G Bairappa, a 75-year-old applicant. . He had approached the Assistant Commissioner stating that he is being neglected by his daughter Girija and son-in-law Y Chandru. . Bairappa had executed a release deed in respect of 1.30 acres of land at Hunasekatte village in Bhadravathi taluk. . Challenging the order passed by the Assistant Commissioner, Girija and her husband argued that Bairappa had in fact sold the property to them. They claimed that Rs 7.25 lakh was paid, and the balance amount was agreed to be paid in six months in terms of the agreement of sale dated July 31, 2023. . It was argued that there was no condition in the release deed that they must look after Bairappa instead of the property received from him. On the other hand, Bairappa questioned the authenticity of those documents. . After perusing the materials, the court said that it is not at all convinced by the documents placed by the petitioners. . Citing the apex court decision in the RBANMS Educational Institution vs B Gunashekar, Justice Suraj Govindaraj directed the present matter to be referred to the Chief Commissioner, Income Tax Department, since the case involves claims of substantial sums of cash being paid. . Duties of registering authorities . The court said that the registering authorities should take appropriate care to ensure that an executant understands the nature and legal effect of the document and that the applicable registration requirements are satisfied. . “The state government may also examine whether administrative guidelines, consistent with the Registration Act, 1908, and the applicable rules, would assist registering authorities in dealing with documents executed by senior citizens, particularly where substantial property is transferred or relinquished in favour of close relatives,” the court said. . It added that the matter is left to the state for consideration in accordance with law and within the scope of its statutory and policy-making powers.

briefs.headline: Karnataka voter roll drops by nearly 1 crore, Gen Z makes up 20% of electorate
briefs.deck: The special intensive revision of electoral rolls in Karnataka resulted in a reduction of 99.76 lakh electors. The final electoral rolls revealed a total of 4.55 crore eligible voters by October 27. Women made up a majority of the electorate, surpassing men by 3.7 lakh. Many electors were marked absent, shifted permanently, or marked as dead and duplicates. The Election Commission processed a net…
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: The special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Karnataka concluded Tuesday, with the final electoral rolls showing an overall reduction of 99.76 lakh electors from the pre-SIR rolls, with the electorate shrinking from 5.54 crore on June 16 to 4.55 crore on Oct 27. At 2.29 crore, women outnumber men by 3.7 lakh, putting the gender ratio at 1,017 women per 1,000 men.
While the overall decline after SIR is of nearly 18%, Chief Electoral Officer Anbu Kumar said: “The net deletions from the list are about 73 lakh, considering only shifted and absent electors. The rest, about 27 lakh electors are categorised dead, duplicate or refused to sign.”
The largest category among electors whose enumeration forms were not submitted was those who had permanently shifted residence, accounting for 65.45 lakh of the 1.08 crore electors left out of the draft rolls. The second-largest category was absent electors, at 19 lakh. This category includes electors who also refused to sign documents, according to the CEO’s explanation.
The list also included 16.39 lakh dead electors and 7.09 lakh duplicate or already-enrolled electors. In addition to the 1.08 crore electors classified as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate (ASDD), Kumar told mediapersons that 61,960 electors who had been issued notices were marked ineligible for the final rolls after hearing. 
He said these included foreign nationals.
On the other hand, the Election Commission added a net 8.19 lakh electors during the claims-and-objections phase, after processing applications under Forms 6, 7 and 8.
“While it is hard to say how many of the ASDD-categorised electors came back to the final list, there have been about 8.19 lakh net additions after the draft rolls,” Kumar said.
ECI data showed that the period between the draft and final rolls saw 10.08 lakh additions, 1.88 lakh deletions and 8.96 lakh modifications. The CEO’s office also presented figures showing that the Commission removed 1.24 lakh permanently shifted electors through Form 7 generated automatically following applications for shifting under Form 8, and another 61,960 electors in the “ineligible” category.
Apart from these, 184 electors were marked absent and 762 duplicate entries were removed during the claims-and-objections process.
Responding to allegations of bulk applications under Form 7, including forms generated in the names of Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) and Assistant EROs, Kumar said none of the bulk applications had been accepted by the ECI, either online or offline.
Chief electoral officer Anbu Kumar said election officials had not generated Form 7 suo motu.
Asked why the reason for deletion was left blank in cases where Form 7 applications were filed by EROs and AEROs, Kumar said electors had been marked “ineligible” by officials concerned on grounds relating to citizenship or other eligibility criteria, following verification during the notice and hearing phase. Form 7 was generated on the basis of speaking orders.
1.7L+ applications beyond deadline
Data from the CEO’s office showed that 1,78,175 applications for additions and deletions were processed after the Sept 23 deadline for filing claims and objections.
While 19.5 lakh applications for additions, deletions and modifications under Forms 6, 6A, 7 and 8 were received within the deadline, the CEO said more than 21 lakh applications were processed for the SIR exercise. This included an additional 89,570 Form 6 applications and 1.29 lakh Form 7 applications.

briefs.headline: Mangaluru man goes missing in Israel
briefs.deck: M’luru man goes missing in Israel
briefs.bodyText: Shadrak Emmanuval (41), a resident of Kodakkal in Padil-Kannur, Mangaluru, who is employed in Israel, has been missing for the past 12 days. He has neither reported for work nor contacted his family, prompting his relatives to urge the Union government to take steps to trace him. . The family has submitted appeals to Dakshina Kannada MP Capt Brijesh Chowta, Mangaluru City Police Commissioner and the Indian Embassy in Tel Aviv, Israel, seeking assistance in locating him. . Shadrak had travelled to Israel on May 16, 2025, on an employment visa after securing a job through a recruitment agency in Mangaluru. He was working at UCT Liquid Solutions, a construction company in Nof HaGalil, near Nazareth in northern Israel. . He regularly spoke to his family over WhatsApp calls. On October 16, he spoke to his family for around 22 minutes, after which contact with him was lost. He has not reported for work since then. Repeated attempts by his family and friends in Israel to reach him have failed, increasing their anxiety. . “His call got disconnected while we were speaking on October 16 night. Since then, my son has not answered our calls,” his mother, Ratna, told reporters on Tuesday. . DK MP Capt Brijesh Chowta said he had written to the Union Minister for External Affairs, bringing the matter to his attention. He added that Indian Embassy in Israel was making efforts to locate Shadrak and that he had also spoken to the Consul General of Israel in Bengaluru.

briefs.headline: Kodachadri ropeway back on track, forest & wildlife nods likely in a yr
briefs.deck: Kodachadri ropeway back on track, forest & wildlife nods likely in a yr
briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: The ambitious passenger ropeway project linking Kodachadri hills in Shivamogga district with Kollur in Udupi district is back on track, with forest and wildlife clearances expected within a year, according to National Highways Logistics Management Limited (NHLML). . The project gained momentum after local residents and environmentalists opposed a proposal to widen the existing 3-metre, 9-km road. . NHLML has engaged Nagpur-based K&J Projects Private Limited to prepare the detailed project report (DPR) and is confident of securing the statutory clearances. . “DPR preparation is at a preliminary stage and we have formally approached the forest department seeking necessary clearances. The project screening committee (PSC) has given its go-ahead,” a senior NHLML official told DH. . The project will require forest clearance following the committee’s approval. It is expected to use about 9.35 hectares of forest land, for which the government will provide 12.45 hectares of revenue land for compensatory afforestation, the official said. .Kodava hockey utsava returns: Chenanda Cup to host 383 families in Napoklu. “We will use forest land without cutting any trees,” he said. . Authorities are also preparing a wildlife conservation and mitigation plan to protect local flora and fauna and reduce human-wildlife conflict. The ecologically sensitive area is home to the endangered lion-tailed macaque. . The proposal will then move through the Deputy Conservator of Forests (DCF) and the Karnataka State Board for Wildlife (SBWL) before reaching the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL). . “Forest and wildlife clearances are part of DPR preparation. We will float construction tenders only once stage 1 clearance is obtained,” the official noted, referring to the forest department’s in-principle approval. . He described the clearance process as “crawling”. . The project will be implemented under a public-private partnership (PPP) model where a private player will make the initial investment and build the ropeway under a build-own-transfer (BOT) arrangement. The Centre will provide viability gap funding (VGF) of up to 40%, the official added. . Meanwhile, NHLML has paused a similar passenger ropeway project at Mullayanagiri, Karnataka’s highest peak in Chikkamagaluru district. . In October 2025, the agency invited bids to prepare the DPR, but did not award the contract, as existing connectivity options were considered adequate. . A pre-feasibility study conducted years ago yielded unsatisfactory results. However, NHLML may take up the project in the future, the official said. . The state budget for 2027-28 has proposed a ropeway connecting Kaimara, Seethalayyanagiri and Mullayanagiri. . Vehicles can travel to Seethalayyanagiri, a peak 3 km below. Visitors then have to hire a jeep to reach the base of Mullayanagiri. The final journey to the peak is a short trek. . stories.headline: Garbage dumped at Kalpalli crematorium in Bengaluru
stories.deck: The garbage trucks sport a banner of Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, a month-long campaign launched in September. Residents allege that each vehicle has a picture of S. Raghu, C.V. Raman Nagar BJP MLA, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
stories.bodyText:
Several garbage trucks have been dumping dry and wet waste at Kalpalli crematorium for nearly three months now, alleged families living on the premises and around it. These trucks bear the banner of Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, a campaign to mark Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 25 years in power, residents claimed. However, S. Raghu, C.V. Raman Nagar BJP MLA, denied that garbage is being dumped there.
The crematorium is home to 17 families from the Kalpalli burial ground and two from the electric crematorium. Many live in makeshift shelters on the premises, including those who work as grave diggers. The waste is dumped around their homes, near the crematorium’s registrar’s office and on the crematorium premises, they say.
Seva Sankalp Abhiyan
These trucks sport a banner of Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, a month-long campaign launched in September. Each vehicle has a picture of Mr. Raghu and Mr. Modi, residents alleged.
However, Mr. Raghu dismissed the claims, saying that only wood from felled trees and leaves are taken to the crematorium to make manure, and no other waste is dumped there. He said people may have misused his name. He said he would be the “last person” to be involved in such dumping and that he had instead been asking everyone to cooperate and dispose of garbage responsibly.
Residents flag issues
Residents said that from 7 a.m. until late in the evening, sometimes until 7 p.m., at least two garbage trucks arrive every hour. The waste includes sanitary waste and wood cuttings, along with dry and wet garbage, they alleged.
Residents stated that the stench reaches their homes, making it difficult to live there. “We have shown them that children and senior citizens live here. People are cooking beside the waste, living and sleeping there. But when we try to stop the trucks, the people who come to dump the garbage threaten that they will take away our jobs,” a resident said.
“The dumping has also upset families who visit the burial ground to pay their respects to deceased relatives on anniversaries and other occasions,“ residents lamented, pointing out that garbage is being dumped on and around graves, leaving families to see piles of waste as the first thing when they visit.
A resident of the crematorium said the dumping had left them helpless. “Some families have accused us at the electric crematorium of taking money to allow people to dump garbage here. It is our duty to maintain cleanliness, but we do not know why this is being done to us. Garbage is being dumped even around our homes,” he said.

stories.headline: SC gives green signal for Blue Line project work in Bengaluru’s Hebbal
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: In a relief for Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation (BMRCL) Limited, 
Supreme Court
 has permitted it to proceed with construction of its ongoing Blue Line in Hebbal. A bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva gave this clarification after hearing a petition filed by BMRCL, pointing out that the status quo order passed on May 4 will not come in the way of ongoing Metro work.
The apex court is hearing a special leave petition filed by Lakeview Tourism Corporation, which had challenged the high court’s April 10 order, quashing the acquisition of 55 acres and 13 guntas of land made in its favour. Calling it a monumental fraud, HC had directed a CBI investigation into the issue.
BMRCL claimed 84% of work has been completed for the Blue Line project and any delay will cause huge losses to the state exchequer.

stories.headline: Construction costs up 33%; Builders in Bengaluru face margin squeeze as sales slow down
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: Realty-related construction costs have risen about 33% while sales have slowed, squeezing builders in 
Karnataka
. Reason: Tamil Nadu’s ban on transporting construction materials such as M-sand, P-sand, aggregates and ready-mix concrete, extended till Jan, has cut stone, sand and jelly supply to about 40%, with a crushers’ shutdown adding to the strain.
Builders said there has been a shortage of sand and jelly, while cement and steel prices are 8-10% higher. Sand prices have risen from Rs 250-300 to Rs 450-800 per tonne, nearly doubling costs. Over 70% of Karnataka’s stone crushers and another 15-20% near the Tamil Nadu border, around Krishnagiri, are affected by supply disruptions.
Farook Mahmood, president emeritus, Bangalore Realtors Association India (BRAI), said: “The four-month Rera extension offers some relief, but projects could face delays of at least six months, as the Tamil Nadu ban extends until Jan 2027. Construction costs could rise by Rs 250-400 per square foot. Builders are sourcing materials from neighbouring states or available market stocks at higher prices. Builders are not even insisting on realistic prices at this stage; they need supplies to complete projects. Delays will affect homebuyers, who may have to pay both pre-EMIs and rent while waiting for possession.”
BRAI said it had been discussing the issue, while contractors’ associations were expected to take it up with the govt.
Suresh Hari, partner, Vishal Promoters & Builders, said: “Under Rera, we cannot revise prices once committed. When material costs rise, builders must absorb losses or delay sales, with buyers ultimately bearing indirect price hikes. We can source materials in advance, but then storage and holding costs go up. At present, we have stored in advance and managed, but in the long term, there needs to be a regulatory mechanism.”
Builders seek govt intervention and their key demands include resolving the double royalty issue, allowing compliant crushers to operate for extended hours, coordinating with the Tamil Nadu govt to permit royalty-paid materials with e-permits in border districts, deferring premium and approval fees for three months, expediting approvals and publishing a revised summary schedule of rates.
Ramani Sastri, director, Sterling Developers, said: “The gap in all construction products is widening and the projects are slowing down considerably. The cost of construction has gone up by about 15 to 18% and is likely to go up further. Rera extension can only help soften penalties of delays and nothing else.”
Confederation of Real Estate Developers’ Associations of India (Credai) said the industry welcomes and encourages measures to bring costs down. The body said it has had a meeting with the govt officials scheduled next week. Quarries and aggregates are under pressure, while the sector is also looking at alternatives in paints, tiles and sanitaryware, all linked to petrochemicals. In Morbi, Gujarat, more than 200 building material units have reportedly been shut, adding to supply concerns.
Bhaskar T Nagendrappa, president, Credai Karnataka, said: “The cost has gone up initially during the western Asia conflict, but now the recent ban has fueled more. We will meet with the govt and express our concerns and solutions.”

stories.headline: Bengaluru’s electorate plunges from 1.03 crore to 59 lakh after SIR
stories.deck: The final electorate comprises 28,68,670 male voters, 30,40,431 female voters and 674 third-gender voters.
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru has lost more than 43 lakh names from its electoral roll in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), with its electorate shrinking from 1.03 crore to just 59.08 lakh. The city, which accounted for the highest number of deletions in Karnataka during the draft stage, was also disproportionately affected during the subsequent notice and hearing process, with nearly half of all notices issued across the State concentrated here.
The final electorate comprises 28,68,670 male voters, 30,40,431 female voters and 674 third-gender voters.
At the draft stage, Bengaluru’s electorate had already plummeted to 56.99 lakh. Despite a month-long window for claims and objections, the final roll saw a net addition of only 2,74,372 names, leaving the city with slightly over 59 lakh electors against its pre-SIR electorate of over one crore.
The scale of the deletions remains shocking across the city’s districts. For instance, in BBMP North, the pre-SIR electorate fell from 23,32,621 to just 13,25,284 in the final roll. Even Bengaluru Urban, which had 40,21,039 electors before the exercise, now has just over 24 lakh. Across the city, the final roll reflects a massive reduction in the electorate, with additions doing little to offset the names struck off during the revision.
Most of the Assembly constituencies across Bengaluru were the epicentre of the notice phase as well. Of the 43.82 lakh notices issued across Karnataka over logical discrepancies and lack of mapping, nearly 24 lakh were concentrated in the city. Of these notices in Bengaluru, 65,881 cases resulted in net deletions from the final roll, including 28,834 people marked as “ineligible“ following hearings.
Moreover, at least 12 of Bengaluru’s 28 Assembly constituencies have seen the number of names deleted from the draft electoral roll exceed 10 times the winning margin in the 2023 Assembly election.
Bommanahalli, Dasarahalli, and B.T.M. Layout — all three Assembly constituencies reported more than 50% net deletions.
Bommanahalli, for instance, had reported the highest deletions following publication of the draft rolls, with more than 54% of names deleted. This constituency had 4.84 lakh names when the exercise began. Following publication of the draft rolls, its electorate fell to just 2.19 lakh. Then, within this drastically reduced electorate, another 1.02 lakh received notices. The final roll figure for the constituency stands at 2,24,339.

briefs.headline: Construction material shortage post TN ban hits Blue Line work in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: At a time when 
Namma Metro
’s opening timelines are already facing delays, Tamil Nadu’s continued ban on transporting stones and construction aggregates to other states has impacted work on the Blue Line, affecting the supply of key construction materials.
A senior Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) official said contractors executing the 58-km Blue Line, connecting Silk Board with Kempegowda International Airport, are facing difficulties in procuring construction materials. While construction of the elevated corridor between Silk Board and KR Pura is at an advanced stage, work on KR Pura–KIA stretch is still on.
“Contractors said 30 to 40 per cent of construction materials would be sourced from crushers in Tamil Nadu’s Krishnagiri district before the ban. Shortages of quarry dust, crushed stone and aggregates have affected several activities, including concreting, architectural finishing and other construction works,” the official said.
The shortage has also affected depot construction, particularly the availability of railway ballast required for track laying. Along Outer Ring Road (ORR) stretch, multiple activities, including construction of entry and exit structures and travelators, are under way.
“The ban has disrupted construction activity over the past three months,” said an engineer with a construction company executing works on ORR. “Earlier, we were procuring aggregates from Hosur, which had around 14 quarry-crusher units supplying materials. Following the ban, supplies were disrupted for months, forcing vendors to shift procurement to just 4-5 crusher units in Bidadi. Aggregate prices, which were around Rs 800 per tonne earlier, have more than doubled now. This has added to the financial strain on contractors executing big projects,” the engineer said.
Karnataka Truck Owners’ and Agents’ Association president GR Shanmugappa said the restrictions affected not only Metro construction but also several other infrastructure projects in Bengaluru. “More than 40,000 tonnes of stone were being transported to the city before the ban; 600 to 700 truck owners have been affected now.”
I
nsetWhy the restrictions?
Tamil Nadu had imposed restrictions citing rising domestic demand, inadequate supplies and escalating prices of construction materials. The move was also intended to curb illegal mining and unauthorised transportation of stone materials. The restrictions, which came into effect on July 27 for an initial three-month period, have continued.

briefs.headline: Gen Z accounts for 20% of Karnataka electorate, emerges as key vote bank
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: The special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which removed 99 lakh voters from the lists, has revealed a significant shift in 
Karnataka
’s voter demography, with Gen Z emerging as an important electoral force.
According to the final electoral roll data released by the Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer’s (CEO) office on Tuesday, the state has 86,56,838 voters aged between 20 and 29. Another 6,83,364 first-time voters have been added to the revised rolls, taking the total number of voters aged 18 to 29 to 93,40,202.
This puts the younger electorate at nearly 20% of Karnataka’s voter population, making it a significant vote bank for political parties ahead of the 2028 Assembly elections and the 2029 Lok Sabha polls.
Gen Z voters are concentrated largely in urban centres, including Bengaluru, Belagavi, Mysuru and Kalaburagi. Bengaluru Urban district leads with 10.5 lakh voters in the 20-29 age group, followed by Belagavi with 7.9 lakh, Mysuru with 4.4 lakh and Kalaburagi with 4.2 lakh.
The numbers could prompt political parties to reassess their electoral strategies, particularly amid protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and growing Gen Z-led demonstrations. 
The younger electorate could play a decisive role in determining electoral outcomes in the coming years, marking a departure from the traditional focus on the working-age population.
However, voters aged between 40 and 59 continue to form the largest and most influential demographic, with a population of around 1.7 crore.
Questions also remain over the accuracy of age-related data in the electoral rolls. Discrepancies in voters’ recorded ages across age groups persist, with electors flagging errors that the 
Election Commission of India
 (ECI) did not rectify during the SIR exercise.

briefs.headline: Nelamangala villages near Bengaluru on edge as Leopard sightings rise; Cub rescued
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: Frequent leopard sightings in Nelamangala taluk on the outskirts of Bengaluru have triggered panic, with villages reporting attacks on pets and livestock. In two separate incidents Tuesday, a month-old male cub was rescued from a field at Mallarabanavadi, while CCTV footage from Soladevanahalli captured a full-grown leopard prowling near houses and hunting domestic animals in daylight.
The cub was spotted by villagers near a clump of bushes in farmland. Believed to be barely a month old, it was found whimpering alone, apparently after being separated from its mother. Villagers secured the cub and alerted the forest department. A team led by Nelamangala range forest officer 
Manjunath
 shifted the cub to Bannerghatta Rehabilitation Centre for further treatment.
Meanwhile, residents of Soladevanahalli are on edge after CCTV footage showed a leopard moving close to residential properties and preying on domestic animals. Locals allege that leopards have been frequently straying into residential areas, targeting pet dogs and livestock. Forest officials attribute the increased sightings to the leopard population in nearby wooded areas and agricultural patches. The animals are believed to be venturing closer to human settlements in search of easy prey.
Concerned about the potential threat to residents, villagers have petitioned forest department officials to deploy baited cages and capture the leopards.

briefs.headline: Karnataka SIR: Final electoral roll out on October 27; net additions remain minuscule
briefs.deck: The final roll will have around 4.54 crore voters, with one crore names struck off the rolls
briefs.bodyText:
After more than three months of a clean-up drive under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, Karnataka’s final electoral roll will be published on October 27. The list will be uploaded on the website of the Chief Electoral Officer, Karnataka.
The exercise, which began with the stated aim of ensuring that no eligible voter was excluded and no ineligible voter remained on the rolls, led to the deletion of 1.07 crore names across the State. Karnataka had 5.54 crore voters when the exercise began. The final roll will have around 4.54 crore voters, with one crore names struck off the rolls. Details on the number of ineligible voters identified, or the count of foreign citizens — another stated aim of the SIR — remain unknown so far.
During the draft roll stage, 16.39 lakh names were deleted on the ground that the voters were dead, while over seven lakh were identified as duplicate entries. Another 3.83 lakh names were deleted under the “Others” category, which is not seen in many other States that conducted the SIR. Even as the exercise comes to an end, the CEO’s office has not clearly explained what the “Others” category comprises, apart from stating that it includes people who refused to sign.
However, the largest category of deletions — 80.62 lakh names — comprised voters who had shifted residence or were not found at their addresses during the enumeration phase. Unlike those identified as dead or duplicate, these voters were not necessarily ineligible to vote. They would have had to apply through Form 6 to have their names restored to the rolls. Yet, only 7,87,534 applications for inclusion were received, a figure that also includes applications from new voters.
The scale of deletions under the SIR has not been offset by additions in any constituency across the State, with applications for inclusion falling far short of the number of names struck off the draft roll.

NEW DELHI: Following up on GST Council decisions, Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs has issued over half a dozen detailed circulars on steps to reduce litigation and appeals, issuing show cause notices to taxpayers and speeding up registrations and changes that businesses need to make. stories.headline: On the question of KIIFB’s future
stories.deck: An expert panel constituted by Keralam’s UDF government to review the functioning of KIIFB has recommended winding it up and absorbing its functions into the State government, prompting a closer look at the merits of off-budget borrowings by States and the need to boost public investment in Keralam
stories.bodyText:
In July, Keralam’s newly elected UDF government set up an expert panel to review the functioning of Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB). The panel, headed by a former civil servant, was tasked with recommending measures to restructure KIIFB and strengthen the government’s institutional capabilities, among other things. The committee has recently submitted its report, which has been tabled in the State Assembly.
Apparently critical of KIIFB’s functioning, the committee has recommended winding it up; absorbing its functions and capabilities into the State government, news reports say. The principal reason for the panel’s recommendation is that with the clubbing of KIIFB’s borrowing function with the State budget, the special purpose vehicle (SPV) has lost its primary purpose.
A disputed investment model
KIIFB, restructured by the LDF government, reportedly boosted the State’s infrastructure investment by raising extra-budgetary resources, including securing soft loans known as “Masala Bonds” from international agencies after the disastrous floods of 2019. However, the SPV’s functioning and financial performance have remained contentious. The comptroller and auditor general’s (CAG) strictures against KIIFB have become a convenient beating stick for the Centre and the Opposition parties in the State. Leftist critics have branded it as the arm of “the Left Managerial State” for promoting controversial projects, bypassing legislative approvals. In the fog of the debate, KIIFB’s original purpose and economic principles underlying it seem to have been lost sight of. We seek to explain them, intending to shed some light on the contentious issue.
Though Keralam has sound traditional transport infrastructure such as road network and rail connectivity, it lags behind in modern facilities, such as high-speed railways or highways, especially when compared to the neighbouring States. Keralam reportedly spends a mere 1.5 per cent of the Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) on infrastructure. This was so in spite of Keralam’s own-tax revenue to GSDP ratio being among the highest among major States, as per the RBI data.
KIIFB was set up in 1999 and underwent a major restructuring in 2016; the institution’s record in expanding public goods is apparently well acknowledged. However, its functioning raised many queries. The CAG found that the SPV’s finances flouted its procedural audits, which became a sticking point between the Centre and the State. Moreover, as KIIFB functioned outside the purview of the State budget, without generating financial profits from its lending, its borrowings being serviced out of the State’s revenue became the heart of the contention.
Rationale for off-budget borrowing
In the good/bad old days of “planning”, State finances broadly followed the “gap-filling” approach; meaning the Centre made up the difference between a State’s projected revenue growth and its “developmental needs” as per the State plans. It was a negotiated process, part financial and part political. Evidence shows that richer and politically influential States got the lion’s share of the divisible pool of the plan resources.
The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (FRBM) 2003 changed that by seemingly imposing a “hard budget constraint”, with the fiscal deficit capped at 3 per cent of GSDP. The RBI now monitors the size of the State debt. The coupon (interest) rate of the State loans depends on the State’s debt sustainability measures. The hard budget constraint has reportedly improved State finances, or at a minimum, made them transparent.
However, most States have devised a variety of means for securing extra-budgetary resources, or off-budget borrowings (OBBs) – as evident from the RBI’s compilation of State finances. The CAG, tracking OBBs, finds that there is a bewildering variety of them. And the actual OBBs are far higher than what it is able to count, as per its own findings. In other words, ensuring fiscal discipline seems like a cat-and-mouse game between the Centre and States. Incidentally, Keralam is not among the worst offenders.
Globally, a variety of financial institutions and fiscal arrangements have existed outside of the budgetary process. Numerous kinds of para-statal organisations are a feature – not a bug – of the fiscal landscape, especially among fast-growing Asian economies. China, for instance, has a bewildering variety of financial arrangements that enable provinces to draw resources from the national development banks to sustain employment at the local level, augment production and exports and ensure political stability. No wonder, China’s public debt to GDP ratio is nearly 300 per cent – though most of it domestic.
Then, realistically, what should be the rules for managing extra-budgetary resources and institutions for Keralam? Simply speaking, if extra-budgetary resources are productively used and they comply with the government expenditure principles, having such off-budget institutions/borrowings may not be undesirable. This follows the Domar rule: so long as the output growth rate exceeds the interest rate on such loans(either at current or at constant prices), they are being used productively. Since such investments have a public good character, individual projects may not be yielding adequate revenue or covering the full costs. However, if in the aggregate they contribute to growth in state output (GSDP) and follow the Domar rule, then such investments are in principle viable.
However, if the State-level SPVs borrow from external sources for social purposes or green financing, which usually have lower interest rates for longer maturities, they need to be assessed differently, as they involve exchange rate risk. Given Keralam’s fragile ecology and need for substantial low-cost resources for protecting it, external borrowing for such purposes by creating SPVs may be desirable, as KIIFB reportedly proved to be after the floods in 2019. The expert committee’s recommendation to dissolve KIIFB is the easier part. In the present political milieu, efforts to boost public investments to catch up with the neighbouring States are a harder job – with the Centre strictly monitoring Keralam. The State will have to devise newer and administratively innovative means to tap OBBs, as most States do. The task is primarily a political one.
(R. Nagaraj is an economist.)

stories.headline: RBI Governor asks states to adopt prudent borrowing strategies
stories.deck: Addressing the 36th Conference of State Finance Secretaries, the governor also advised states to make effective use of the State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC) forum
stories.bodyText:
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) advised State governments to adopt prudent borrowing strategies and ensure quality spending, highlighting the importance of long-term fiscal health.
Addressing the 36th Conference of State Finance Secretaries, the governor also advised states to make effective use of the State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC) forum.
The Conference was attended by the finance secretaries of 27 States and three Union Territories as well as senior officials from the Union Ministry of Finance, Controller General of Accounts and the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, RBI said in a release.
Mr. Malhotra highlighted the importance of maintaining the quality of expenditure to ensure the long-term fiscal health of the states.
He also emphasised the need for states to adopt prudent borrowing strategies and efficient cash management practices.
The Governor urged the states to onboard onto the Unified Lending Interface (ULI) and utilise Programmable Central Bank Digital Currency (P-CBDC) for Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT).
The meeting reviewed, inter alia, market borrowings by the sates, short-term financial accommodation to the states from Reserve Bank, and adoption of Benchmark Issuance Strategy by the states.
During the Conference, the Governor also released a booklet titled 'Compendium on Cash and Debt Management for State Governments' which summarises relevant concepts, operational processes and good cash and debt management practices in a concise and accessible format.

India open to free, fair trade with China: Piyush Goyal
briefs.bodyText:
HAGUE: India is open to promoting free and fair trade with China and hopes to expand its exports of goods and services to the neighbouring country and Asean region in the coming years, commerce and industry minister 
Piyush Goyal
 said late Monday, signalling scope for deeper trade engagement with Beijing.
Goyal told reporters that India believed in open trade across the world and was looking for open markets in different countries on a reciprocal basis to sell Indian goods and services. “Yes, at some stage maybe we will do that also,” he said when asked if India was considering a similar exercise with China after concluding talks on a trade agreement with the European Union (EU).
The minister said he had met his Chinese counterpart in Yaoundé, Cameroon, earlier this year and again in New Delhi during the latter’s visit for the Brics summit in Sept. “We are open to working and encouraging free and fair trade with every country around the globe. We are looking to open markets in different countries on a reciprocal basis for our goods and services also,” he said.
As China supplies India with a number of critical intermediate goods and important raw materials, Goyal said there was an established judicial process that could be followed if it was ever found that the pricing of a particular good was not proper. 
“We believe in the rules of fair play, we believe in the rules of open trade across the world. Markets are open across the world. We welcome suppliers to meet the growing needs of India,” the minister said.
Asked about China’s recent export controls on tunnelling equipment, which could impact several infrastructure projects, Goyal said he had learnt about the move after leaving India and that govt would work on the issue.
According to commerce department data, China became India’s largest trading partner in the first half of the current fiscal year, with bilateral trade between the two countries rising 10.5% to $91.8 billion, with the trade deficit also expanding.
While India has recently implemented trade deals with the UK and New Zealand and the EU agreement is expected to open markets in 27 European countries, Goyal said talks with Chile were nearing conclusion and those with Canada were making good progress. Mexico is keen on an “early-harvest” arrangement while negotiations with the South African Customs Union have just begun. He said India was working towards securing preferential access to economies accounting for 76% of the estimated $115 trillion global GDP.

briefs.headline: Government identifies 120 items for local production push
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Government has identified around 120 products, including intermediates and capital goods, for domestic manufacturing push and to reduce dependence on imports, with a separate plan for tunnel boring machines in the works after China imposed restrictions on their shipments.
As part of the exercise, which is being driven by the department for promotion of industry and internal trade (DPIIT), the range of products includes chemicals such as acetic acid, pharmaceutical products and inputs, medical technology related items, machine tools, including some textile looms, construction equipment, cranes, products used in the aerospace sector as MROs (maintenance, repair and operations) are coming up in the country. Besides, the list also includes some consumer goods, including products that are part of the footwear value chain, persons familiar with the discussions told TOI.
While discussions are currently underway with other govt agencies, three types of intervention are planned. One, short-term protection that will enable products, which are identified, to deal with competition from overseas, especially China, till supplies are diversified. 
A similar strategy had been adopted in the case of mobile phones in the initial years.
The second set of measures will deal with cost disability through incentives that could be capital incentives or phased over a period and may be linked to turnover. Also, on the menu is the option to provide R&D assistance as some of the products need to be developed locally as technology is not available.
Over the last six-to-eight years, govt has sought to provide support to companies, both domestic and international, across sectors ranging from pharma and electronics to semiconductors, solar power equipment and white goods to encourage local production. A large part of the money has flown through PLIs, along with two semiconductor missions as well as a scheme aimed at enhancing production of electronic components in the country as demand for inputs has soared after domestic manufacturing of phones took off. Support for R&D probably flows from the experience in battery production as companies that have begun “local production” are essentially importing cells from China and selling battery packs as the entire production chain and technology is controlled by companies across the border. A similar experience was seen in the case of solar panels.
The plan flows from govt’s overall 
Atmanirbhar Bharat
 strategy, which has received renewed attention after the West Asia crisis, when several critical items were in short supply locally due to large import dependence. Even during Covid, supply of several products, including medical inputs, was hit as China controlled the production chains.

briefs.headline: India would have grown 8% but for external shocks: RBI
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: India would already have been an 8% growth economy if it had not been grappling with an exceptionally difficult global environment, 
Reserve Bank of India
 (RBI) deputy governor Poonam Gupta said, arguing that improvements in digital infrastructure, public services, manufacturing and governance have strengthened the economy's capacity to withstand external shocks.
"We would have already been a 8% growth economy but for the external shocks," Gupta said during a fireside chat at a BFSI event organised by Business Standard. The economy's resilience reflects years of work on strengthening systems, advancing digitalisation, improving transparency in public services and making state govts important partners in growth, she said.
India's challenge now is to sustain that progress and raise its growth rate from around 7% to 8% or more in an environment marked by global uncertainties.
External environment itself could provide a significant boost if conditions improve. "Now suppose this global environment becomes better, if not right away, in the next one year, another 50 basis points to one percentage point growth will come just from them," she said, referring to the potential contribution of a more favourable global environment.

briefs.headline: IRDAI to implement distribution reforms only after consensus: Ajay Seth
briefs.deck: Speaking at the annual Business Standard BFSI Insights Summit, Ajay Seth said the regulator will work to expedite claims in case of health policies
briefs.bodyText:
Amid concerns over the impact of the proposed changes in insurance distribution, IRDAI Chairman Ajay Seth on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) assured the industry that the regulator will implement the reforms only after reaching a consensus.
Speaking at the annual Business Standard BFSI Insights Summit, Mr. Seth said the regulator will work to expedite claims in case of health policies.
Mr. Seth said he has been meeting people extensively since the release of the discussion paper on distribution reforms to hear out the industry's concerns.
"I'm in the listening mode, hearing what the concerns are…," he said, adding that the release of the paper has generated a necessary dialogue around the insurance sector's role and the changes that are required.
"I'll attempt to build consensus for the reforms needed for the sector and for our economy," he added.
Regarding concerns around commissions proposed as part of the new proposals, Mr. Seth said the paper suggests higher commissions initially as the amount of efforts required to sell a policy is much higher than the efforts needed at the time of renewal.
Commenting on the online insurance aggregators, Mr. Seth said such entities play an important role, but they also tend to take up other work like having a physical distribution channel eyeing the penetration gap, and also questioned the need for having dynamic pricing.
He also questioned the need for sharing personal details before a premium structure is shared, including the insistence on excluding their telephone numbers from 'do not disturb' lists.
On the issue of portability, Mr. Seth rued that the activity is concentrated in a very small set of entities, pointing out that the commissions paid may be playing a role in customer behaviour.
Highlighting that 60% of the port-ins activity was concentrated in three entities, reflecting customer choice for better insurer, Mr. Seth said the same set of entities also accounted for 20% of port-outs.
"If a large number of people were so convinced about the good quality, people with them should not have been leaving out. So what is at play? The commission is driving behaviour from one to another," he said.
Mr. Seth also said that we need to learn from what has succeeded in the country, and the best practices from the banking and capital markets industry needs to be picked up by the insurance sector as well.
He said that there is no information available on the amount of time taken for a hospital admission or discharge to be done in the case of a health policy and added that this will be an area of focus for IRDAI going forward.
The career bureaucrat-turned-regulator added that the health insurance sector has "maximum dissatisfaction" levels among the customers.
Mr. Seth said that he sees the Bima Sugam, a marketplace for insurance, launching in the next 30 to 45 days, starting with a motor insurance offering.
Stressing on the need to have a relook at how we assess the industry's performance, Mr. Seth advocated a move away from the concept of looking at penetration in favour of number of lives covered and how effective is the cover for every rupee of premium paid.
General insurance has been growing at about 1.3 times the growth in nominal GDP while life is at par with nominal GDP growth, Seth said.

briefs.headline: Fresh bad-loan generation may rise in FY27; private banks face greater pressure: Report
briefs.deck: Ratings agency Icra expects the trend of relatively higher loan slippages at private sector banks to continue in the second half of FY27, even as credit costs are projected to remain favourable and significantly below historical levels
briefs.bodyText:
Fresh non-performing assets (NPA) in the banking sector are likely to increase in the current fiscal, with private sector banks expected to face relatively higher pressure due to their exposure to unsecured retail and micro, small and medium enterprise loans, according to a report released on Tuesday (October 27, 2026).
Ratings agency Icra expects the trend of relatively higher loan slippages at private sector banks to continue in the second half of FY27, even as credit costs are projected to remain favourable and significantly below historical levels.
According to the rating agency's estimates, the fresh NPA generation rate for public sector banks is projected at 0.8 per cent in FY27, while that for private sector banks is estimated at 2.5%.
In absolute terms, fresh NPA is estimated at ₹1 lakh crore in FY27 for state-owned banks and ₹1.3 lakh crore for private banks, according to a report.
The agency attributed the relatively higher slippages at private sector banks over the past two years to their higher share of unsecured retail and MSME loans.
Despite the anticipated increase in fresh bad-loan generation, Icra expects the banking sector to maintain healthy profitability, supported by favourable credit costs and adequate capitalisation.
The agency projected the banking sector's gross non-performing assets (GNPA) ratio at 1.7-1.8% by March 2027 from 1.7% in June 2026. The net NPA ratio is expected to remain at 0.4-0.5% against 0.4% in June 2026.
Icra expects bank credit growth to remain healthy at 15.1-15.9% in FY2027, translating into incremental credit of ₹32.3-33.8 lakh crore.
Credit growth stood at 15.9% in FY2026.
However, geopolitical risks and inflationary pressures could pose challenges to its growth estimates, the agency said.
Sustaining healthy domestic deposit growth after the deployment of available liquidity will also remain a key monitorable for banks in the second half of the fiscal.
The reversal in the interest-rate cycle could support banks' net interest margins (NIMs), which had faced pressure during the declining rate cycle.
The agency expects yields on advances to reprice faster than deposit rates, supporting a recovery in margins.
Rising bond yields could also influence corporate borrowing decisions and support bank credit demand. However, the sustainability of the pickup in corporate lending will depend on whether the gap between bank lending rates and bond yields narrows, it added.
Separately, Icra expects non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) to maintain double-digit growth, with assets under management (AUM) projected to expand by 15-17% in FY27 and 14-16% in FY28.
However, borrowing costs are expected to rise. The cost of the outstanding debt stock could increase by up to 0.30%, while the average cost of funds in FY27 is projected to rise by 0.10-0.20%.
NBFCs and housing finance companies together will require additional funding of ₹6.9-7.1 lakh crore in FY27 to support growth and refinance existing or maturing borrowings.

briefs.headline: L&T Q2 PAT rises 33% to ₹5,202 crore, revenue up 16%
briefs.deck: L&T’s consolidated order book stood at ₹8,53,514 crore as of September 30, 2026, up 15% from March 2026. International orders accounted for 54% of the total order book, providing substantial revenue visibility.
briefs.bodyText:
Larsen & Toubro (L&T) reported a 33% year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated profit after tax (PAT) to ₹5,202 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, supported by strong revenue growth and robust order inflows.
Consolidated revenue rose 16% YoY to ₹78,750 crore, driven by accelerated execution across its Projects, Products & Manufacturing (PPM) businesses. International revenue stood at ₹45,870 crore, accounting for 58% of the total.
The company secured orders worth ₹1,47,665 crore during the quarter, registering a 28% YoY increase. Major orders came from Hydrocarbon – Offshore & Onshore, CarbonLite Solutions, Public Spaces & Airports, and Power Transmission & Distribution businesses. International orders amounted to ₹92,375 crore, contributing 63% of total order inflows.
L&T’s consolidated order book stood at ₹8,53,514 crore as of September 30, 2026, up 15% from March 2026. International orders accounted for 54% of the total order book, providing substantial revenue visibility.
“The Company has delivered a strong quarter in an everchanging geopolitical landscape. This performance reflects continued customer confidence and our ability to secure large and complex orders across sectors and geographies,” said S N Subrahmanyan, Chairman and Managing Director, L&T.
R Shankar Raman, President and Whole-time Director (Finance), said the company witnessed an all-round performance despite geopolitical challenges. “We are maintaining our guidance,” he said.
Subramanian Sarma, Deputy Managing Director and President, said recent developments in Saudi Arabia had not affected L&T’s operations or project sites, which continued to function as usual.

stories.headline: Mitchell Starc equals Dale Steyn, leaves several legends behind in elite list
stories.deck: Mitchell Starc made headlines with his stellar 20th five-wicket haul in Test cricket, claiming 6/72 against South Africa. His fiery spell ignited a collapse in the opponent's batting lineup, shifting the momentum dramatically. From a strong position at 203/1, South Africa crumbled to 329 all out, intensifying the series, which now stands at 1-1, underscoring the match's importance.
stories.bodyText:
Mitchell Starc
 produced a devastating spell to claim his 20th five-wicket haul in Test cricket, helping Australia stage a remarkable comeback against South Africa on the opening day of the deciding third Test at Newlands on Tuesday.
The left-arm pacer returned figures of 6/72 as South Africa collapsed from 203/1 to 329 all out after appearing firmly in control of the contest. His latest haul also took his tally of five-wicket hauls in international cricket to 29, placing him alongside 
Dale Steyn
 among the most prolific fast bowlers in the format.
Starc now has 20 five-wicket hauls in Tests and nine in ODIs. He has moved to the top of the list of active fast bowlers with the most five-wicket hauls in Test cricket, ahead of 
Kagiso Rabada
, who has 17, and Jasprit Bumrah, who has 16.
In the all-time list of fast bowlers with the most five-wicket hauls in international cricket, Starc sits sixth, behind Richard Hadlee (41), Glenn McGrath (36), Waqar Younis (35), James Anderson (34) and Wasim Akram (31).
South Africa had looked set for a commanding first-innings total after openers Aiden Markram and Marques Ackerman added 140 runs. Ackerman made 95 off 94 balls, while Markram scored 78 as the hosts reached 203/1.
However, Starc triggered a dramatic collapse, removing David Bedingham for 50 and Wiaan Mulder for a duck in quick succession. After South Africa recovered through a 95-run seventh-wicket partnership between Marco Jansen and Ryan Rickelton, Starc returned with the second new ball to dismantle the tail.
He dismissed Rickelton for 42 before bowling Jansen for 52. Starc then claimed Gerald Coetzee and Kagiso Rabada for consecutive golden ducks, completing a stunning turnaround as South Africa lost four wickets in six balls.
His figures of 6/72 were also his best against South Africa in Test cricket, improving on his previous best of 6/154 in Perth in 2012.
The series remains level at 1-1, with the third Test set to determine the winner.

stories.headline: 'That's why I praised my team': Sammy backs WI's 2-2 draw, calls India 'dangerous'
stories.deck: West Indies coach Daren Sammy praised his team's performance in the recent T20I series against India. The West Indies managed a commendable 2-2 draw against the formidable Indian team on their home ground. Sammy emphasized the challenges posed by India's batting power and smaller boundaries during their matches. He acknowledged the progress made by his team despite facing tough opposition.
stories.bodyText:
West Indies head coach Daren Sammy has reiterated his praise for his team's 2-2 T20I series draw against India, pointing to the challenge of competing against the reigning two-time T20 world champions after India's record-breaking batting display against New Zealand. Sammy highlighted the impact of smaller boundaries, batting-friendly pitches and the challenges posed by a wet ball for bowlers as he underlined why India remain such a formidable opponent in the shortest format.
India produced a breathtaking performance in the third T20I against New Zealand, chasing down a target of 199 in just 13.2 overs to secure a six-wicket victory and take an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series.
Abhishek Sharma and teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi set the tone with a blistering 133-run opening partnership off just 7.1 overs. Abhishek smashed 113 off 38 balls, while Sooryavanshi contributed 45 from 19 deliveries, leaving the depleted New Zealand bowling attack with little room to recover.
Reacting to India's dominant display, Sammy took to X to reinforce his earlier assessment of the West Indies' performance against India.
"Wow…. That’s why I praised my team for what they accomplished in India. India is a dangerous team.
"1. Smaller boundaries
"2. Batting paradise pitches
"3. Wet ball for bowlers," Sammy wrote.
'We probably didn't have a chance': Sammy on West Indies' series draw
West Indies managed to hold India to a 2-2 draw in their recent five-match T20I series, with the final match in Bengaluru abandoned due to rain. Sammy had described the result as a significant achievement for his side, which competed against the defending champions on their home turf.
"It's a true reflection of how all the teams have played, especially for our guys," Sammy had said after the washed-out fifth T20I.
"I'm pretty sure when the series started, we probably didn't have a chance. But that was just the opinion of others."
The West Indies coach also emphasised the progress his team had made, pointing to their ability to challenge India and outperform them in certain aspects of the series.
"We understand what success means to us; we don't ever take for granted where we are as a team and the challenges that we face. We just look to make those strides, and I think after this series we've taken a massive step," he added.
"We played against the defending champions, and we've matched them (and) in certain areas we've outplayed them, especially in their backyard."
Abhishek, Sooryavanshi power India to record-breaking chase
India's performance against New Zealand offered a striking illustration of the batting firepower Sammy had highlighted. The hosts were unable to contain Abhishek and Sooryavanshi, who attacked from the outset and put the chase firmly in India's control during the Powerplay.
India raced to 118 without loss in the first six overs, recording the highest Powerplay total by a Full Member nation in men's T20 internationals. The previous benchmark was Romania's 116 for no loss against Serbia in 2021.
The Indian batters also crossed the 100-run mark in just five overs, the second-fastest team hundred in men's T20 cricket, behind Eswatini's effort against Mozambique earlier in 2026.
India reached their fifty in just 2.2 overs, equalling the fastest team fifty recorded in men's T20 cricket. Papua New Guinea had achieved the same feat against Vanuatu, while Romania also reached the milestone in 2.2 overs against Serbia.
Abhishek's 113 off 38 balls, featuring nine fours and 11 sixes, was the standout contribution, while Sooryavanshi's aggressive start ensured the required run rate never became a concern. India eventually completed the chase with 40 balls remaining.

stories.headline: WPL auction: Sneh among biggest names in the fray
stories.deck: There are only 27 available slots — including 20 reserved for the Indians
stories.bodyText:
By the time the first name comes up at the WPL’s mini-auction on Wednesday, the third ODI between India and Zimbabwe would have reached somewhere around the halfway mark in Vadodara. India’s middle-order batter Tejal Hasabnis is likely to be curious about what is happening at Grand Hyatt here.
She is one of the 146 players who will go under the hammer. In the only chance she got in the Zimbabwe series, she may have lasted only five balls, but last month she had done really well for India-A against the touring Australia-A.
So Tejal should interest some of the franchises. There could be even more interest in Sneh Rana, the off-spinning all-rounder released by Delhi Capitals.
Sneh is, in fact, among the biggest names at this auction. Others include Australia’s T20 World Cup-winning captain Sophie Molineux, her compatriots Grace Harris and Jess Jonassen, Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu and England opener Sophia Dunkley.
Among the capped Indian players are G. Kamalini, Kiran Navgire, Uma Chetry, Taniya Bhatiya, Saika Ishaque, Asha Sobhana, Priya Mishra, Titas Sadhu and Saima Thakor.
There are some interesting names among the uncapped Indians, too. Like the 16-year-old Ira Jadhav, who last year smashed an unbeaten 346 off 157 balls for Mumbai against Meghalaya in the Women’s Under-19 One-Day tournament. There are only 27 available slots — including 20 reserved for the Indians.
Going into the auction, UP Warriorz could well be a bit more excited, and anxious, than the other four franchises. Warriorz have the biggest purse of ₹3.75 crore. That is a lot more than Gujarat Giants (1.25 crore), Royal Challengers Bengaluru (1.15 crore), Delhi Capitals (1.1 crore) or Mumbai Indians (90 lakh).
It would be fascinating to see how Warriorz try to turn the auction into a mega opportunity.
